So far just wearing it around the house and doing some jumping, running, bending over, and squatting I have to say I am quite impressed. It seems well put together and I have not felt the gun would come loose or fall out. I don't have a proper belt yet so it sags more than I would like, but that is not the fault of the holster. Following are pictures with a Sig Sauer SP2022

Covered with my overly large shirt pulled as tightly as possible. It is very difficult to see but the grip is noticeable just where the red meets the orange at the middle-right of the picture.

Uncovered on belt.

Sitting on desk you can see the trigger is completely covered.

And here you can see how far down the kydex goes as well as the texturing on the holster.

The tools provided make it extremely easy to adjust the gun position to my liking. I am fine with the standard 15 degree cant it comes with. However I did play around with moving the clips up and down to figure out how high I like it to ride in my pants. This takes all of 15 seconds to do. I figured out the stock configuration is what I prefer.

As for the kydex. It seems solid enough. I did have to loosen it a bit to make holstering and drawing a bit easier. The gun slid in fine but it was a bit too tight to holster when I was wearing it. So I loosened it up and got it working smoothly with just enough retention to hold it in place until I purposefully draw the firearm. I assume when I get a proper belt I will have to readjust the tension.

A word of caution here. The included paperwork recommends blue loctite on all the screws when you finally get everything adjusted perfectly to keep things from loosening up. I won't do this until I have a proper gun belt and have ensured I am happy with the placement of everything. Next on my list is my cwp class next week. Once that's done and I have my license to carry (as it is required in my state) I expect this holster will work wonders. It gets hot here in the south and the material it is made of seems like it would do well with sweat.
